title: Parcel locker platform
summary: Product design for robotic parcel lockers, from kiosk touchscreens to the back office that runs the network.

meta.label: Platforms
meta.value: Kiosk touchscreens, mobile app, web back office, AR tooling

meta.label: Scope
meta.value: UX, UI, design system, enterprise software redesign

sections.heading: Parcel lockers
body: Cleveron builds robotic parcel lockers that carry packages from the warehouse to the customer's hands. My work covered that whole journey: the touchscreens people use to send and receive parcels, the courier app, the mobile app for home-locker owners, the office software companies use to manage parcels, lockers, invoices and allocations, and internal AR tooling that showed assembly workers which parts to pick next.

sections.heading: Office software and design files
body: The office software expected people to read a 40-page PDF manual before they could use it. Design work had no shared component library, so the same interface pieces were rebuilt for every project.
sections.pull: The goal: office software that explains itself.

sections.heading: Design system
body: One of my first moves was getting the team onto Figma and building a component library from scratch for the existing software. Shared components let us build and ship changes quickly, since each piece was designed once. It also freed up my time for a proper redesign of the office software.

sections.heading: Office software
body: Many of its features were too complicated to understand, and some had no explanation at all. I rebuilt it around the tasks people actually do, like slot allocation, with a more logical page structure and labels that walk them through each step. The other goal was a more contemporary, premium look.

sections.heading: Courier app
body: Couriers pick up and deliver parcels between lockers and the robots inside them. I mapped that flow and prototyped the app they use on the route.

media.caption: Courier app flow. Scroll sideways to follow it.

sections.heading: Home locker app
body: Cleveron also sold a home locker, a parcel locker for a private house, and I designed the app that came with it. The main screen was one large button to lock and unlock the locker. Notifications told the owner when a parcel was delivered or picked up, and a history listed every parcel movement with the service provider that handled it.
